config.title: Token Refresh with Axios Interceptor

intro.title: Token Refresh with Axios Interceptor
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a secure React application that automatically refreshes an expired authentication token using Axios interceptors. You will learn how to intercept HTTP requests and responses to check for token expiration and silently request a new token without disrupting the user. The core programming concepts involve using Axios instances, request/response interceptors, and managing asynchronous API calls. You'll implement this in a TypeScript React project, creating a reusable service that handles token refresh logic to keep users logged in.
intro.usecase: Token refresh interceptors are essential in any application that requires persistent user authentication, such as banking dashboards, e-commerce platforms, or productivity tools like Notion. When users spend extended time in these applications—editing documents, analyzing financial data, or browsing products—their access tokens expire silently in the background. The interceptor automatically refreshes tokens without disrupting the user's workflow, preventing sudden logout during critical operations. This pattern ensures seamless experiences in admin panels, data visualization tools, and collaborative editors where uninterrupted sessions are crucial.

objectives: Construct an Axios instance with custom configuration for API requests
Apply Axios interceptors to modify request headers before they are sent
Implement response interceptors to handle API error responses
Execute conditional logic to detect authentication errors based on status codes
Define a refresh token function that makes a POST request to obtain new tokens
Utilize async/await syntax to manage asynchronous token refresh operations
Store and retrieve authentication tokens from browser storage (localStorage/sessionStorage)
Control request retry logic by intercepting failed requests and refreshing tokens
Modify request headers to include refreshed access tokens before retrying
Handle race conditions by implementing request queueing during token refresh
Return appropriate error responses when token refresh fails or credentials are invalid
Apply TypeScript interfaces to define types for authentication tokens and API responses

steps.title: Create axios instance
steps.instruction: Create an axios instance with a baseURL configuration. Place it inside your App component, before the return statement.

steps.expectedOutcome: An axios instance is created with a configured baseURL, ready for API calls.
successCriteria: The code should include an axios.create() call with a baseURL property set to a string URL.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created an axios instance with a baseURL configuration. This instance will be used for all API calls in your app.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using axios.create() with a configuration object that includes a baseURL property.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on creating the axios instance. Use axios.create() with a configuration object containing baseURL set to a URL string.

steps.title: Add request interceptor
steps.instruction: Add a request interceptor to your axios instance to automatically attach the access token to outgoing requests. The interceptor should set the Authorization header to 'Bearer ' followed by the current accessToken value.
steps.hint: Use the axios instance's .interceptors.request.use() method. The interceptor function receives a config object and should modify its headers.Authorization property before returning the config.
steps.expectedOutcome: The axios instance now has a request interceptor that automatically adds the Authorization header with the current access token to all requests.
successCriteria: The interceptor should be added using .interceptors.request.use() and should set config.headers.Authorization to a Bearer token string using the accessToken state variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a request interceptor that will automatically attach the access token to outgoing requests.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an interceptor, but it might not be correctly setting the Authorization header. Make sure you're using the accessToken state variable and formatting the header as 'Bearer ' + token.
steps.feedbackWrong: The request interceptor hasn't been added correctly. You need to call .interceptors.request.use() on your axios instance with a function that modifies the config headers.

steps.title: Add response interceptor for token refresh
steps.instruction: Add a response interceptor to your axios instance that handles 401 errors. Use the `api.interceptors.response.use` method to add the interceptor.
steps.hint: Call `api.interceptors.response.use` with two arguments: a success handler and an error handler. For now, just add the structure - you'll implement the 401 handling logic in the next step.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your axios instance will have a response interceptor structure ready to handle 401 errors in the next step.
successCriteria: The code should call `api.interceptors.response.use` with two handler functions (one for success, one for error).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the response interceptor structure. This sets up the foundation for handling 401 errors and token refresh.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling `api.interceptors.response.use` with both a success handler and an error handler function.
steps.feedbackWrong: Remember to add a response interceptor using `api.interceptors.response.use`. You need to provide two handler functions as arguments.

steps.expectedOutcome: You should have an async login function that makes a POST request and updates both token states with the response.
successCriteria: The function must be named 'login', be async, use the 'api' instance for a POST request, and call both setAccessToken and setRefreshToken with data from the response.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the login simulation function that will handle initial authentication and token setting.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function is async, uses the 'api' instance, and updates both token states with setAccessToken and setRefreshToken.
steps.feedbackWrong: The login function is missing or incomplete. Remember to create an async function named 'login' that makes a POST request with the 'api' instance and updates both token states.
